title: Proof strategy: three mechanisms for $q$-deformed regularity
html:
Remark. Proof strategy: three mechanisms for q-deformed regularity

The proof of global regularity rests on three mechanisms, each exploiting q > 1.

Step 1: Exponential UV damping. The q-Laplacian eigenvalues [k]_q^2 grow as q^{2k}/(q-q^{-1})^2 for large k (Kelvin dispersion). Mode k dissipates at rate \gamma_k = \nu_q [k]_q^2 / L_q^2, growing exponentially in k. The enstrophy \Omega(t) = \sum_k [k]_q^2 |\hat{v}_k|^2 satisfies d\Omega/dt \leq -\nu_q [1]_q^2\Omega + C\Omega^{3/2}. At q = 1 the damping coefficient vanishes; at q > 1 it provides a linear restoring term.

Step 2: Finite cascade depth. The Planck--Reynolds number \mathrm{Re}_q = 2/(q-1) bounds the active modes: N_{\mathrm{eff}} \leq \lfloor \log_q(\mathrm{Re}_q^{3/4}) \rfloor < \infty. The q-NS equation reduces to a finite-dimensional ODE, globally well-posed by Picard--Lindelöf.

Step 3: Bootstrap to smoothness. Higher modes are damped to zero in finite time. Parabolic regularity on the truncated system gives v \in C^\infty for t > 0. Initial regularity extends by uniqueness.

Mechanism Role Failure at q = 1
Exponential eigenvalue growth UV regularisation [k]_1 = k (polynomial)
Positive viscosity \nu_q > 0 Enstrophy damping \nu_1 = 0
Finite cascade depth Dimensional reduction N_{\mathrm{eff}} \to \infty

The dissipation term 2\nu_q\sum_k [k]_q^2 |\hat{v}_k|^2 in the energy inequality converges absolutely for q > 1 because [k]_q^2 |\hat{v}_k|^2 decays faster than any geometric series. This absolute convergence — absent at q = 1 — is the analytic content of the exponential UV cutoff.
